styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts favour the candidate: 12 visible tones per tile against 3 for grass and 7 for paving, and 0% near-flat coverage. By eye the piece is only about 2 tiles wide and a few pixels tall. It reads as a pale horizontal bar with two orange-brown end caps, more like a plank or sign than steps cut into a cliff. The treads show about 4 lightness steps against the 5-6 in the references. They have no per-stone shading or grain like the paving's individually shaded stones. The edges mix dark tinted pixels with neutral grey-black ones (41% near-neutral), which leans toward the sticker look. The tread highlights are crisp but there is little material texture, so the piece looks thinner and flatter than the paving reference at the same scale. When in doubt, fail.
